findings.failureScenario: photo.reject and crop.rotateAspect are both engine commands declared with shortcut X, so in handle() one X press pushes both ids into `fire` (bindable loop, lines 360-370). With the Crop panel open, the photo.reject entry is redirected to crop.rotateAspect (line 509-511) and the crop.rotateAspect entry is NOT skipped (line 513 only skips it outside Crop), so it falls through to app.run at line 559. Pressing X once runs Rotate Crop twice: the aspect is swapped and swapped back (net no visible change) and two 'Rotate Crop' undo steps are recorded. The existing test library_keys_yield_to_search_and_crop_context only asserts the flag stays None, not that the crop rotated once. (Declarations: crates/engine/src/cmd/library.rs:718 and crates/engine/src/cmd/develop.rs:784, both Some("X").)
findings.action: Make exactly one of the two fire entries act in the Crop panel: e.g. at line 509 `continue` without running (letting the crop.rotateAspect entry run), or skip the crop.rotateAspect entry when photo.reject is also in `fire`; add a test asserting X in Crop swaps the crop aspect exactly once and adds one undo step.
findings.sourceQuote: // X is both reject (library) and swap crop aspect (crop tool)

findings.failureScenario: The `cull` closure discards the result of app.run (line 400 only uses it for advance). The P/X/U and 0-5 key paths then toast 'Flagged as Pick' / 'Flagged as Reject' / 'Unflagged' / 'Rated ★★★' unconditionally (lines 435-440, 456-460). When the command fails (e.g. photo.pick's has_selection precondition with nothing selected, or a catalog write error), the user is told the photo was flagged/rated although nothing changed.
findings.action: Have `cull` return the run result and only show the success toast when it is Ok (toast the error otherwise).

semanticReview.reason: The code's own stated contract for the shared X key (CONTEXTUAL partners disambiguated by context in handle) is violated in the Crop panel, and cull key feedback reports success regardless of outcome.
